title: External TXT import crashes when a file URI cannot be opened
symptom: On the Pixel 8 / Android 14 emulator, launching the app through `ACTION_VIEW` with `file:///sdcard/Download/ancient-construction.txt` after pushing a real corpus TXT to `/sdcard/Download` crashed the app. Logcat showed `java.io.FileNotFoundException: /sdcard/Download/ancient-construction.txt: open failed: EACCES (Permission denied)` from `ExternalImportHandler.extractPayload(ExternalImportHandler.kt:35)`, followed by `AndroidRuntime` force-finishing `MainActivity`.
root_cause: ExternalImportHandler treated third-party external intent URIs as readable once their file name or MIME type looked like TXT. `ContentResolver.openInputStream(uri)` can still throw `FileNotFoundException`, `SecurityException`, or `IllegalArgumentException` for file URIs without grants, missing files, inaccessible providers, or malformed URIs. The exception escaped a Compose `LaunchedEffect`, terminating the app instead of rejecting the unsupported import payload.
fix: Wrap external URI display-name lookup, MIME-type lookup, and byte reading in small safe helpers.
Return `null` from `extractPayload` when an external URI cannot be queried or opened, allowing the app to consume the intent without crashing.
Keep the existing FileProvider + grant success path unchanged.
Add an instrumented regression that verifies an unreadable `ACTION_VIEW` file URI returns `null` instead of throwing.
failed_attempts: Do not rely only on the successful FileProvider import instrumentation path; it has a valid URI grant and does not cover real external file URIs that Android denies.

Do not treat `am start` success as evidence that import succeeded or failed safely; the original crash happened asynchronously after `MainActivity` launched and only logcat exposed the root exception.
impact: Prevents malformed, missing, or permission-denied external TXT imports from crashing the reader app and keeps real external-share/open flows fail-safe.
